title: Shock
summary: Shock is a life-threatening failure of the circulation, often from blood loss, severe burns, infection or a severe allergic reaction. Treat the cause, lay them down and keep them warm.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} – shock is a medical emergency
when: Any signs of shock after injury, bleeding, burns, allergy or illness
They become confused, drowsy or unresponsive

steps.title: Lay them down
steps.text: Help them lie flat on their back. If there is no suspected injury to the legs, hips or spine, raising the legs may be considered.
points: Someone with breathing difficulty may be more comfortable sitting up

steps.title: Keep them warm
steps.text: Cover them with a blanket or coat, and insulate them from the cold ground. Loosen tight clothing.

steps.title: Reassure and monitor
steps.text: Stay with them. Check breathing and response regularly and be ready to start CPR.

warningSigns: Pale or grey, cold, clammy skin
doNot: Do not give food or drink
Do not let them walk around

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
